result.reason: 5 findings, 1 of them important for behavior (F1) and 3 important for missing tests (F6), plus 1 nit; 3 candidates dropped.

findings.label: F1
findings.problem: In #addSelected, the waiting stops with no selected place are always pushed after the free time and the drive to the next selected stop. A waiting stop shows at its set time, and that time can be earlier than the free time and drive. When it is, scheduleOf() returns entries out of time order. The comment says this order 'keeps the entries in time order', and the domain model says the list is in time order.
findings.failure_case: I ran timelineOf on this day: stop A runs 3:00 to 4:00 p.m., then dinner set for 5:00 p.m. with no place yet, then dessert set for 8:00 p.m. with a 20-minute drive. The result lists free time from 4:00 to 7:40 p.m., then the drive from 7:40 to 8:00 p.m., then dinner at 5:00 p.m., then dessert at 8:00 p.m. Dinner comes after entries that start almost three hours later than it does.
findings.label_reason: The schedule does something other than what the code says (time order), and a user can plainly reach it by setting a meal time with no place picked before a later set-time stop. It's not D1 because running the code shows the failure. The change added this code.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: scheduleTimeAt() returns null for any minute at 2 * MINUTES_IN_DAY or later. That is a new rule, and no test checks it. The Moab stargazing test only reaches the next day, which is below the cap.
findings.failure_case: You could delete the `minute >= 2 * MINUTES_IN_DAY` check, or change it to 3 days, and every test would still pass.
findings.label_reason: The change adds behavior a caller can see (empty times past the second day), and no test would fail if it were removed. Nothing above F6 fits, because the code does what it says.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: townName() falls back to place.address when a place has no name, and locationOf() uses it. That is new behavior, and no test checks it. The locationOf test uses only places that have names.
findings.failure_case: You could replace `place.name ?? place.address` with `place.name ?? ""`, and the tests in calendar.test.ts would still pass.
findings.label_reason: The change adds a visible result with no test that checks it. The code is right, so F1 to F4 don't fit.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: openTimeInMinutesOf() returns null when the day has no date, and when the stop's timeline entry has no start or end minute. Both rules are new, and no test checks them. The only null test is for a stop with no selected place.
findings.failure_case: You could delete `date === null` from the guard, or the entry.startMinute/endMinute null check, and every test would still pass. The non-null assertion in the openMinutesWithin call would then need a fallback, but no test reaches that path.
findings.label_reason: The change adds behavior callers can see, the null result before there's a start date or before the leg is re-routed, with no test of it. The code itself isn't wrong.

findings.label: NF1
findings.problem: #driveMinutesOf only compares the leg with the day's selected stop places. It doesn't compare leg.routedFromPlace or leg.routedToPlace with fromPlaceOf() and toPlaceOf(). If a write changes where the day starts or ends, such as selecting a stay's lodging, the old leg's drive times are still used until the leg is re-routed at the end of the write.
findings.failure_case: In one write, a stay's hotel is selected, and then approveOpeningHours reads openTimeInMinutesOf for a stop on the next day. The drive times come from the leg that was routed from the town, not from the hotel. So the recorded open minutes can be off.
findings.label_reason: This only happens partway through a write that changes a day's end place and also reads its schedule. Nothing in the app does that today, so it isn't normal use. The change added this code.

dropped.problem: Waypoints on a leg would add segments, so segmentDriveTimesInMinutes.length would never equal selected.length + 1 on a day with waypoints, and every time would come out empty.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: The Leg in domain-model.md line 796 says waypoints don't split a segment, and LegsService sends them as pass-through points. So the segment count is always the number of selected stops plus 1.

dropped.problem: For seasonal averages, an empty list of current dates passes dates.every(), so text written for dates wouldn't count as out of date once the dates are gone.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: Once the itinerary has a start date, it can't be cleared. setStartDate takes only a CalendarDate, and the start date is kept, so datesOf() can't go back to empty after weather text is written.

dropped.problem: An always-open period returns end - start regardless of any other periods, so a list with both kinds would count minutes twice.
dropped.label: NF1
dropped.reason: Google gives the always-open period as the only period, so this input has no source in the app. That makes it a note, and the code is new, so it would be a nit. I dropped it as too speculative to act on.
